blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Xerophytes adapt to arid conditions using thick cuticles, sunken stomata, and reduced leaves or spines to minimize transpiration.
Hydrophytes develop specialized aerenchyma tissue that provides buoyancy and facilitates gas exchange in aquatic environments.
Halophytes thrive in saline environments and feature unique negative geotropic respiratory roots known as pneumatophores.
Viviparous germination is a distinctive characteristic of mangrove vegetation, allowing seeds to germinate while attached to the parent plant.

blocks.content: Halophytes exhibit viviparous germination, where seeds germinate while still attached to the parent plant.

rows: Thick cuticle, sunken stomata, spines, CAM pathway
Aerenchyma tissue, poorly developed roots, stomata on upper surface
Well-developed root systems, broad leaves, normal stomata

items: Pneumatophores (breathing roots) and Vivipary are frequently asked traits of Halophytes/Mangroves in UPSC and State PSC exams.
Sunken stomata and CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism) pathway are crucial xerophytic adaptations to reduce water loss.
Aerenchyma tissue presence is a signature identification feature of Hydrophytes.
